terra.problem: The prayer compares the king to rain; it does not compare the righteous to grass growing after rain.
The rain image does not establish that the righteous will not struggle or that things are growing rather than wilting.
The prayer does not say everyone stays put or gets better.
The prayer asks named kings to bring tribute and gifts, not the whole world to bring something.
Even as a guess, 'they came' treats the requested gifts as an event that already happened.
'The kings did bring gifts' treats the prayer's request as an event that already happened.
'I'd want that to be false too' assumes what the baker wants.
The verse gives the reason for their redemption, but it does not state whether the oppressed pay for help.
Grain growing on hilltops does not by itself establish that there is plenty to go around.
Grain on the hills does not establish that the whole country has plenty.
